what_it_states: alpha-local DP (all-pairs likelihood-ratio bound, Eq. 2-3) for non-interactive Markov kernels on general Polish spaces; objective = Fisher information of the privatized parametric model (one-dimensional parameter in the main optimization, Eq. 21). Continuous staircase/extremal mechanisms q^(mu)(x,dr) = e_x(r) mu(dr) indexed by Radon sub-probability measures mu on the extremal set E = {r: X -> {1,e^alpha}} (Eq. 9-14), with existence of a maximizer imported from its reference [3]. Proposition 1: symmetrization mu^(s) under the swap T(r) = e^alpha + 1 - r is normalized and symmetric. Theorem 1: if the maximizer is symmetric, i^(s) is mu-bar-a.e. constant and the maximum Fisher information equals 2/(e^alpha+1) max_{r in B} i^(s)(r) (attained by a binary two-point mechanism, Remark 3). Proposition 2: symmetric/asymmetric decomposition with alpha^2 versus alpha^3 orders as alpha->0. Section 3.1 / Proposition 3: asymmetric pushforward mechanisms (Lemmas 1-2) recover the full non-private Fisher information as c->0 with c e^alpha -> infinity. Section 3.2: injectivity for c <= 1/2 (Lemma 3), explicit density (35), rejection-sampling implementation and Gaussian-translation simulations. Section 3.3: interpolation to the binomial mechanism as c->1. Section 4: proofs (Choquet representation, weak Hardy-Littlewood maximal inequality for uniform integrability). Cites [13] Geng-Kairouz-Oh-Viswanath for higher-dimensional staircase noise (citation only; not opened under this direction).
what_it_does_not_state: No central (curator-level) additive-noise mechanism for a vector query; no squared-error / MSE objective for additive noise; no l1-diamond or translation-sensitivity body; no all-law pure-DP MSE value or selector; no mixed-cost all-law bound E||Z||_2^2 >= (2/3) inf E||Z||_1^2; its optimality statements are conditional (Theorem 1 assumes a symmetric maximizer) or asymptotic (Proposition 3) and concern Fisher information under LDP.
